key_insight: Finite energy features independent of graph size can control normalized optimization values across bounded-degree graphs for affine tasks, with asymptotic guarantees for general Lipschitz tasks on hyperfinite families.
engineering_relevance: These results identify conditions under which graph models trained on small instances can predict optimization values on larger instances.
method: Bound task-value differences using discrepancies in normalized scalar energy probes.
Use Shapley–Folkman bounds to quantify representation error for general Lipschitz objectives.
Realize energy features with fixed-weight message passing and random node initialization on bounded-treewidth graphs.
evidence_signal: Experiments use exact solvers and trained models to test transfer guarantees; the abstract reports no quantitative results.
watch_item: General Lipschitz tasks can retain nonvanishing representation error on expanders, and prediction guarantees require encoder accuracy, readout stability, and representation coverage.
paper_title: On Sparse Graph Limits for Neural Combinatorial Optimization
